summary: This proposed standard clarifies the instructions given to IANA for the WebSocket subprotocol name registry that was set up by RFC 6455. It is a small administrative fix so that registrations are handled consistently.

plainLanguage.summary: Think of a club's sign-up sheet for nicknames. Some people were unsure how to add a name, so this note makes the sign-up instructions clearer.

subtitle: Clarifying rules for registering WebSocket subprotocol names.

tldr.problem: RFC 6455 created a registry for WebSocket subprotocol names but the instructions for handling case-sensitive names were unclear, causing potential for confusion.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7936 clarifies that subprotocol tokens are matched case-sensitively, and IANA should refuse registrations that differ only by case from existing ones.
tldr.outcome: New WebSocket subprotocol names can be registered with clear rules that prevent similar-looking names from causing confusion.

today: RFC 7936 is a Proposed Standard. It updates RFC 6455 to clarify the WebSocket Subprotocol Name Registry procedures, and both documents together govern how subprotocol names are registered.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 6455 established a registry at IANA for WebSocket subprotocol names and said that IANA should use First Come First Serve registration procedures. However, as other protocols started reusing this registry, it became clear that the instructions about how to handle case sensitivity needed clarification. The subprotocol tokens are matched using case-sensitive string matching, but without clear guidance, registrants might try to register names that differed only in case.
sections.plainLanguage: WebSocket needed a way for different programs to agree on message formats. They set up a name list but forgot to explain how strictly they check the spelling.

sections.title: Clarified Registry Rules
sections.content:
RFC 7936 makes the rules explicit: subprotocol tokens are matched case-sensitively, so xmpp and XMPP are technically different. However, IANA is instructed to decline any registration that differs from an existing one only in case, to minimize confusion. This means if myapp is already registered, IANA will reject MyApp or MYAPP.

The RFC also encourages registrants to consult section 1.9 of RFC 6455 for additional advice on avoiding collisions and choosing good subprotocol names.
sections.plainLanguage: Names are checked letter-by-letter including uppercase and lowercase, but IANA will stop you from registering a name that's just a different capitalization of one already registered.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 7936 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6455. The WebSocket Subprotocol Name Registry now has clear case-sensitivity rules documented by both RFCs.
sections.plainLanguage: This is the official clarification about how WebSocket names are registered and checked.

references.text: Fette, I. and A. Melnikov, "The WebSocket Protocol", RFC 6455, December 2011.
Narten, T. and H. Alvestrand, "Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs", BCP 26, RFC 5226, May 2008.
